analysis: Broad: database design, programming, computing infrastructure and data analysis anchor an option that also addresses digital strategy, organisations, privacy and user-centred product work. Interviews and field evidence support those applied questions. This relates directly to the external degree’s systems, people and organisational scope.

Data: linear algebra, numerical methods, signals and statistical inference build a distinct mathematical spine with advanced algorithms, model validation and deep learning. This develops the documented data direction, including processing, modelling and inference, without claiming to reproduce the Semantic Web.

Human-centred: computing and database fundamentals connect to interviews, perception, attention, social behaviour, design and customer experience. Research synthesis supports judging behavioural evidence. Product design and customer journey work provide evidence of how needs inform design while the UvA course specifically studies software interfaces and usability. The sustained human-centred strand is different from both the broad organisational and mathematical programmes.

Three independently defensible concepts reach the allowed maximum. Responsible technology and digital governance contribute within these options, while the selected courses do not establish a dedicated compliance-architecture sequence. Social Robotics is an unselected comparator choice, and general UCR robotics does not by itself create a human-robot interaction option.

academicConstruction: Resolved all nine original offering conflicts. Consumer Product Design moves to term six, Business & Economy in the Age of AI moves earlier, and Social Psychology moves after Brain & Behavior. Modern Sociology and Psycholinguistics give way to direct user research and evidence synthesis in the human-centred option. All three replace general rhetoric with more direct technical or user-oriented work. Partial alignment uses the actual subjects or methods: for example, UvA Data Science and UCR deep learning share model implementation and evaluation, and UvA Interaction Design and UCR Consumer Product Design share requirements, iteration and prototyping. A generic numerical-methods row does not directly match system dynamics for organisational networks, and business strategy does not reproduce regulatory system architecture.
